name: Salt Lake City
tagline: Where the Greatest Snow on Earth meets a city that eats, brews, and roams with it.
description: Cradled between the Wasatch Range and the Great Salt Lake, Salt Lake City is a high-desert basecamp where powder mornings, canyon trails, and a fast-rising global food scene share the same grid. Pioneer heritage radiates out from Temple Square while State Street's immigrant kitchens, Sugar House's craft dens, and a serious coffee culture write the next chapter. Four world-class resorts sit under an hour from downtown, and Antelope Island's bison herd is a short causeway drive away. It's a walkable, mile-high city that treats the mountains as its backyard.

known_for: The Greatest Snow on Earth and four resorts within an hour
a fast-rising global dining and craft-beer scene
canyon hiking and access to the Great Salt Lake
identity.vibe: Mile-high mountain-town energy with big-city polish and outdoorsy, easygoing locals
identity.best_season: Winter for powder; summer for canyon hiking and Antelope Island

hero.summer: Alpine wildflowers blanket the canyons, Antelope Island's bison graze at golden hour, and the patios stay warm long past sundown.
hero.fall: Cottonwood maples ignite red and gold up the canyons while the valley air turns crisp and clear enough to see every ridgeline.
hero.winter: First chair drops into knee-deep powder before the city's even had its coffee — this is why we call it the Greatest Snow on Earth.
hero.spring: Ski the corn snow up top in the morning, then peel down to blossoming Sugar House and a sunny patio by afternoon.

nexus.radius: 1.5 miles around downtown and Temple Square
nexus.description: Temple Square anchors downtown as Utah's most-visited destination — free to walk, ringed by hotels, restaurants, and TRAX stops, and the natural first bearing for any first-timer getting oriented in the valley.

nexus_grid.title: Temple Square & Downtown
nexus_grid.description: Ten manicured acres of pioneer landmarks, the domed Tabernacle, and gardens — the historic heart, walkable and free.

nexus_grid.title: Cottonwood Canyons
nexus_grid.description: Big and Little Cottonwood climb to Alta, Snowbird, Brighton, and Solitude — powder in winter, wildflower trails in summer, all under an hour up.

nexus_grid.title: Sugar House
nexus_grid.description: The city's craft-and-coffee neighborhood — indie roasters, breweries, and a leafy park that anchors the east side.

nexus_grid.title: State Street Kitchens
nexus_grid.description: The global spine of the valley — Vietnamese, Mexican, Himalayan, and Pacific Island kitchens run by the families who built them.

nexus_grid.title: Antelope Island
nexus_grid.description: A causeway drive onto the Great Salt Lake to free-roaming bison, pronghorn, and some of the widest sunsets in the West.

nexus_grid.title: University District
nexus_grid.description: The U of U hillside — Natural History Museum, Red Butte Garden, and easy trailheads with the whole valley at your feet.

modes.label: Foodie
modes.description: From State Street's immigrant kitchens to award-winning downtown tasting menus — chase the flavors that are putting this valley on the map.

modes.label: Chill
modes.description: Slow mornings over serious pour-overs, a book in Sugar House Park, and patios that make you forget you had a schedule.

modes.label: Romantic
modes.description: Canyon overlooks at golden hour, candlelit tables downtown, and a soak under the stars — the Wasatch does date night right.

modes.label: Adventurer
modes.description: First chair, alpine ridgelines, and trailheads minutes from your hotel — this is the city built for people who came for the mountains.

modes.label: Culture
modes.description: Pioneer history at Temple Square, world-class museums on the U hillside, and This Is the Place — the Crossroads of the West, then and now.

modes.label: Nightlife
modes.description: Local breweries, hidden speakeasies, and live music downtown — the scene's smaller than you'd guess and better than you'd expect.

modes.label: Family
modes.description: Bison on Antelope Island, dinosaurs at the Natural History Museum, and gentle canyon trails — big outdoors sized right for little legs.

transit.from_nearest_hub: Salt Lake City International Airport (SLC) sits just 4 miles west of downtown — a 10-minute drive or a straight 20-minute ride on the TRAX Green Line to the city center.
transit.local_transport: UTA runs TRAX light rail (with a free-fare zone downtown), FrontRunner commuter rail up and down the Wasatch Front, and a bus network; ski-bus routes (UTA and Cottonwood Connect) climb to the resorts in winter. Downtown is very walkable, but a car earns its keep for the canyons and Antelope Island.

side_trips.name: Park City
side_trips.pitch: A former silver-mining town turned world-class ski hub, where a preserved Main Street of galleries and saloons sits at the base of two massive resorts.
highlights: Park City Mountain and Deer Valley
summer alpine coaster and mountain biking

side_trips.name: Bonneville Salt Flats
side_trips.distance: 1.5 hours west toward the Nevada line
side_trips.pitch: A blinding-white expanse of hard salt crust stretching to the horizon — the legendary land-speed course and one of the strangest, most photogenic landscapes in the West.
highlights: land-speed racing history at Speed Week

concierge.name: The Powder Hound
concierge.greeting: Welcome to the valley — you made it to the Crossroads of the West. Take a breath, we're a mile up so the altitude's real, and let's figure out whether you're here to ski, eat, or roam.
concierge.personality: First-chair energy and canyon-wise. Knows exactly when Little Cottonwood gates and which State Street kitchen the locals actually line up for. Gentle about the altitude, honest about the traffic, and always steering you toward the good snow and the better tacos.
concierge.sign_off: Drink your water, respect the canyon, and I'll see you on the first chair. — The Powder Hound
